---
title: "Panel models"
subtitle: "Repeated observations of the same people: random-effects logit"
---

`mecompare` works after panel models such as `xtlogit`. The example uses a 30%
sample of households from the Health and Retirement Study, 2010 to 2020 (the
households whose ID ends in 0, 1, or 2): about 31,500 interviews of 7,800
people aged 51 and older, interviewed every two years. The outcome is depressive
symptoms (four or more of the eight CES-D items).

```{.stata-run}
. use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/hrs_si_2025", clear

. keep if year >= 2010 & age >= 51
(169,991 observations deleted)

. keep if mod(floor(hhidpn/1000), 10) < 3
(76,874 observations deleted)

. generate depressed = cesd >= 4 if !missing(cesd)
(1,821 missing values generated)

. generate poorhealth = srhealthB == 0 if !missing(srhealthB)
(28 missing values generated)

. drop if missing(depressed, poorhealth, marstatB, age, woman, race4cat, collegeB)
(1,959 observations deleted)

. xtset hhidpn year

Panel variable: hhidpn (unbalanced)
 Time variable: year, 2010 to 2020, but with gaps
         Delta: 1 unit

. 
. quietly xtlogit depressed i.marstatB c.age i.woman i.race4cat i.collegeB, re intpoints(60)

. estimates store dep

```

After `xtlogit, re`, the marginal effects are changes in the probability of
the outcome, averaged over the random effect (the default prediction of
`margins`). Age is changed by ten years:

```{.stata-run}
. mecompare, models(dep) amount(10)

Predicting: Pr(depressed=1)
Marginal effects (N_dep=31519)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate         SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
marstatB                         |                                       
    currently m - not curren     |                                       
                             dep |     1     -0.096      0.006      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
age + 10 (centered)              |                                       
                             dep |     2     -0.014      0.003      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
woman                            |                                       
                 woman - man     |                                       
                             dep |     3      0.038      0.006      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
race4cat                         |                                       
         NH Black - NH White     |                                       
                             dep |     4      0.008      0.008      0.315
         Hispanic - NH White     |                                       
                             dep |     5      0.067      0.010      0.000
            Other - NH White     |                                       
                             dep |     6      0.054      0.017      0.002
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
collegeB                         |                                       
    college degr - no degree     |                                       
                             dep |     7     -0.063      0.007      0.000

```

Being married is associated with a 9.6 percentage point reduction in the
probability of depressive symptoms. Ten more years of age are associated with
a 1.4 point reduction, and a college degree with a 6.3 point reduction.

## Comparing two outcomes

The second model predicts fair or poor self-rated health. With two panel
models, `mecompare` combines them with [`suest2`](../../suest2/index.html),
which clusters the standard errors on the panel identifier. Random-effects
models need enough integration points to be combined; these two need
`intpoints(60)`, and `mecompare` says when a model needs more.

```{.stata-run}
. quietly xtlogit poorhealth i.marstatB c.age i.woman i.race4cat i.collegeB, re intpoints(60)

. estimates store health

. 
. mecompare, models(dep health) amount(10)

NOTE: mecompare clusters the standard errors on the highest-level group of the multilevel or panel 
> model(s), so they will differ from the models' own. Fit every model without vce(robust); mecompar
> e supplies the clustering.

Predicting: Default prediction for each model
Marginal effects and cross-model differences (N_dep=31519) (N_health=31519)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate  Robust SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
marstatB                         |                                       
    currently m - not curren     |                                       
                             dep |     1     -0.096      0.006      0.000
                          health |     2     -0.069      0.007      0.000
                      Difference |     3     -0.027      0.008      0.001
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
age + 10 (centered)              |                                       
                             dep |     4     -0.014      0.003      0.000
                          health |     5      0.033      0.003      0.000
                      Difference |     6     -0.047      0.004      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
woman                            |                                       
                 woman - man     |                                       
                             dep |     7      0.038      0.006      0.000
                          health |     8     -0.011      0.008      0.189
                      Difference |     9      0.049      0.008      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
race4cat                         |                                       
         NH Black - NH White     |                                       
                             dep |    10      0.008      0.008      0.317
                          health |    11      0.093      0.011      0.000
                      Difference |    12     -0.086      0.011      0.000
         Hispanic - NH White     |                                       
                             dep |    13      0.067      0.010      0.000
                          health |    14      0.198      0.013      0.000
                      Difference |    15     -0.130      0.013      0.000
            Other - NH White     |                                       
                             dep |    16      0.054      0.017      0.001
                          health |    17      0.074      0.021      0.000
                      Difference |    18     -0.020      0.021      0.346
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
collegeB                         |                                       
    college degr - no degree     |                                       
                             dep |    19     -0.063      0.007      0.000
                          health |    20     -0.164      0.009      0.000
                      Difference |    21      0.101      0.009      0.000

```

Being married is associated with a larger reduction in the probability of
depressive symptoms (9.6 percentage points) than in the probability of fair or
poor health (6.9 points); the difference of 2.7 points has p < .01. Age and
gender go in opposite directions for the two outcomes: ten more years of age
are associated with a 1.4 point reduction in depressive symptoms but a 3.3
point increase in fair or poor health. Women are 3.8 points more likely than
men to report depressive symptoms, while the gender difference in fair or poor
health (1.1 points) is not significant.

A random-effects model mixes differences between people with changes within a
person. The [within-person effects](within-person.html) example separates
them.
